## Chapter Summary

A semantic model is easiest to use and most reliable when it is arranged as a star schema. Fact tables record events at a stated grain, one row for each event, with the keys of the things involved and the amounts to be added up. Dimension tables describe the things, one row for each, with the attributes a reader filters and groups by. The invoice header and its lines, designed in the database to avoid repeating facts, form a snowflake in Power BI, in which the customer reaches the lines only through the header. Merging the header's date, number, and customer key into the lines turns them into one fact table that every dimension filters directly. The invoice number stays in the fact table as a degenerate dimension. The restructured model is accepted only when the Validation page shows the same totals as before.

Relationships in a star are many to one, from the fact table to each dimension, with a single cross filter direction. Setting a relationship to Both can make a number respond to a click while changing what it means, and in a model with two fact tables it can carry a selection from one fact table into the other. Only one path between two tables can be active, so a second date, such as the date a line shipped, is related through an inactive relationship that a measure switches on with USERELATIONSHIP. A date table with one row for every day of full years, marked as the model's date table, gives every visual one calendar and lets the time intelligence functions work. Date and Item are reserved words in DAX, so those tables are written in single quotes.

Explicit measures, written in DAX, name each calculation once, carry their own format and description, and can be used in other measures. A calculated column is stored for each row at refresh, while a measure is calculated for each cell from the rows that the cell's filters keep. Every formula is evaluated in a context. The filter context is the set of filters on a cell, which the relationships carry to the fact table. The row context is the current row of an iterator such as SUMX, where RELATED reaches the one side of a relationship, which is how standard cost is calculated from each line's quantity and its item's cost. CALCULATE changes the filter context: its filter arguments replace existing filters on the same columns, and REMOVEFILTERS removes them, so a share of revenue removes the filter on Item but keeps the year. Used inside a row context, CALCULATE turns the current row into a filter, which is context transition.

DAX query view runs queries against the model without building a visual. A tab of tests, each a query whose result must equal a control total from an earlier chapter, documents the model and shows at once whether a change moved a number. Time intelligence functions such as SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, TOTALYTD, and DATESBETWEEN shift or extend the dates in the filter context. The prior year is blank for fiscal 2024, and an expectation built from the months before a month, not including it, cannot be raised by a spike in the month itself.

The general ledger forms a second star, with Account, CostCenter, and the shared Date table as its dimensions. Its year-end closing entries move each year's revenue and expenses to retained earnings, so a measure over all postings shows a net income of zero. A flag brought from the JournalEntry table in Power Query lets the ledger's base measure exclude the closes. Reversing the sign of debits less credits makes revenue positive and expenses negative, so the income statement by year ties to the net income each closing entry transferred, and the pre-closing trial balance in DAX query view balances at the total of Chapter 6.
